# Overall Project Weekly Summary (Feb 22 - 28, 2026)

This week, Optimism focused on hardening the core infrastructure of the Superchain to ensure it remains secure and reliable as it scales. The team successfully launched a new system for managing network upgrades and resolved critical performance bottlenecks, ensuring a smoother experience for both developers and node operators.

## Executive Summary
The primary achievement this week was the implementation of the L2 Contracts Manager, which simplifies how the network receives updates without interrupting service. Additionally, the team proactively addressed potential stability risks and optimized internal tools to help developers build and test their applications faster.

### Key Strategic Initiatives & Outcomes

**Simplifying Network Upgrades and Security**
*Goal: To make the blockchain easier to update and more secure against technical errors.*
*   Launched the **L2 Contracts Manager (L2CM)** in [ethereum-optimism/optimism](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19111), a vital tool that allows the network to upgrade its internal smart contracts more safely and efficiently.
*   Conducted rigorous "failure analysis" to ensure that when the network updates, it happens all at once or not at all, preventing "partial" updates that could cause bugs ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#18830](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/18830)).
*   Improved the security of the network's "savings account" (DelayedWETH) by using advanced automated testing to find and fix potential edge cases ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19275](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19275)).

**Boosting Developer Productivity and Tooling**
*Goal: To reduce the time developers spend waiting for tests and to support more types of hardware.*
*   Reduced "wait times" for developers by teaching our testing systems to run the longest tasks first, making the overall process much faster ([ethereum-optimism/infra#557](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/557)).
*   Added native support for Apple M-series chips (ARM64), allowing developers on modern Macs to run Optimism software much faster without needing "translation" software ([ethereum-optimism/infra#555](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/555)).
*   Cleaned up the official documentation by archiving old notices and preparing new guides to help developers move away from outdated software versions ([ethereum-optimism/docs#1986](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1986)).

**Ensuring Network Stability and Reliability**
*Goal: To prevent the network from slowing down or crashing during periods of high activity.*
*   Identified and fixed a memory-leak issue that could have caused nodes to crash when searching through large amounts of historical data ([ethereum-optimism/op-geth#768](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/768)).
*   Updated the "Superchain Registry" to ensure all interoperable chains are using the correct, verified settings, which is essential for maintaining a unified ecosystem ([ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry#1199](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1199)).

### Cross-Repository Coordination
*   **Holocene Upgrade Alignment**: Multiple teams coordinated across the `optimism`, `infra`, `ecosystem`, and `docs` repositories to fix how the "Batcher" (the tool that bundles transactions) handles data following the recent Holocene upgrade ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#13169](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/13169)).
*   **Supernode Standards**: Developers across the project are collaborating on a shared "Service Level Agreement" for the Supernode. The goal is to ensure that even if one part of the network is slow, the rest of the Superchain stays online and functional ([ethereum-optimism/optimism#19180](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/19180)).

## Repository Spotlights

### ethereum-optimism/optimism
*   Implemented the **L2ContractsManager (L2CM)** to enable seamless L2 predeploy upgrades ([#19111](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19111)).
*   Integrated the **Karst hard fork** and refined fault-proof testing to improve cross-chain security ([#19250](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19250), [#19254](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19254)).
*   Optimized Rust compilation in CI to prevent "Internal Compiler Errors" and speed up the build process ([#19274](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/19274)).

### ethereum-optimism/op-geth
*   Addressed a critical RPC memory exhaustion vulnerability by aligning with upstream `go-ethereum` fixes ([#768](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/768)).
*   Evaluated a community-proposed fix for historical state fallbacks on full nodes ([#767](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/767)).
*   Conducted Failure Mode Analysis for the L2CM to ensure upgrade atomicity and storage integrity ([#18830](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/issues/18830)).

### ethereum-optimism/infra
*   Introduced runtime-based test sorting to maximize parallelization and reduce CI bottlenecks ([#557](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/557)).
*   Enabled native Linux/arm64 support for `op-acceptor`, improving performance for developers on Apple Silicon ([#555](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/infra/pull/555)).

### ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry
*   Updated prestate entries for `kona-client/v1.2.10-rc.1` to maintain CI stability and registry accuracy ([#1199](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1199)).
*   Provided immediate technical support for node operators regarding `op-reth` Docker image locations ([#19264](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19264)).

### ethereum-optimism/docs
*   Archived legacy Upgrade 18 notices and implemented redirects to maintain a clean documentation site ([#1986](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1986)).
*   Began drafting deprecation guides for legacy components to assist developer transitions ([#1988](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/docs/pull/1988)).
